components.gap: The route presents Theorems I-VI, the projection-filter calculus (Sec. 3), conditions C, H, D/D'/D-bar, the Sec. 8.3 finite-size schedule, the Sec. 9 examples and the Sec. 10.2 questions with written proofs, but these claims of the complete article (Fraisse 1954, pp. 363-388, held NUMDAM PDF read in full) are not presented: (1) Sec. 4.7, pp. 376-377, nn. 7-8: the existence of a countable universal relation for the class of all n-ary relations was announced by A. Lindenbaum (Ann. Soc. Pol. Math. 17 (1938) 124-126, 'relation universelle') and by Fraisse (C. R. 226 (1948) 987-988, 'relation riche'); no such attribution occurs on the route (def:p03-fraisse54-universal, fraisse-1954.tex 195-201, omits it). (2) Sec. 10.1, p. 388, nn. 9-10: the arithmetic-type consequence is obtained 'a l'aide d'un theoreme du a L. Henkin' (Trans. AMS 74 (1953)) for arithmetic types 'au sens de A. Tarski' (Proc. ICM 1950); fraisse-1954.tex 440-449 supplies a compactness proof and speaks of 'the source's arithmetic types' with neither attribution. (3) Sec. 4.1, p. 374 (announced in Sec. 1.1, p. 363): for Gamma_R the class of total orders, Theorem III(1) recovers the fact that every set can be ordered; absent from thm:p03-fraisse54-gamma (fraisse-1954.tex 179-191) and annex 230-238. (4) Sec. 1.1, pp. 363-364: the stated purpose that Theorems III(2), IV, V and VI(2) generalize named order facts (A+B as a common extension of two total orders; one order extending any set of orders; every countable order embeds in eta; eta is the only countable dense order without endpoints); the opening (fraisse-1954.tex 5-17) does not state these generalization claims. (5) Sec. 5.1, p. 377 and Sec. 6.3, p. 380: every infinite homogeneous order is an extension of eta; thm:p03-fraisse54-orders (343-355) and annex 484-486 assert only the countable identification with Q. (6) nn. 1, 2, 5 (pp. 363, 369): the announcement history (C. R. 237 (1953) 508-510 and 540-542; Bull. AMS 59 (1953) 341) and the claim that projection filters and ultrafilters were introduced in the 1953 thesis (Sec. 13) and are expounded differently here. (7) Sec. 7.3, p. 382: the printed counterexample is the unary class taking + at exactly one element ('pour un element de la base et un seul'); annex 336-347 substitutes 'at most one positive element' without recording that it departs from the printed example. (8) Smaller remarks: Sec. 1.4, p. 365, for an infinite total order R, Gamma_R is the class of orders and gamma_R the finite orders; Sec. 3.9, p. 372, for a principal filter, filter-equivalence coincides with map-equivalence; Sec. 4.7, p. 376, eta 'or any countable order extending eta' witnesses condition C for total orders; Sec. 6.3, p. 380, these order facts can also be proved directly from 6.1.
components.basis: Present and compared: Secs. 1.2-1.5 (fraisse-1954.tex 19-108, annex 3-139), Sec. 2 incl. Theorem I cycles and the n>2 coding, chain-host successor/limit cases and the union/intersection of chains of ages (annex 46-139), Sec. 3 projection filters incl. 3.8 and 3.10 (fraisse-1954.tex 110-177, annex 141-228), Sec. 4 Theorems III-IV incl. the ultrafilter joint embedding and minimal-cardinality chain argument (179-191, annex 230-286), Secs. 5-6 (193-228, 343-355, annex 288-320, 462-537), Secs. 7-9 (230-341, annex 322-460), Sec. 10.2 questions and n. 11 (451-465). Failure condition not triggered: embeddings preserve and reflect (lines 26-31), every scheduling, chain-union and back-and-forth case is written (annex 3-17, 81-108, 230-286, 288-320, 358-404). Completeness of the article extent fails only on the omitted claims listed in the gap.

Embedding (injection preserving + and - on all tuples, repeated entries included) at fraisse-1954.tex 26-31; age gamma_R and Gamma_R at 42-55; homogeneity as the ultrahomogeneity of finite structural maps at 203-213 with def:p03-ultrahomogeneous (classification-theory.tex 54-64); HP and JEP as C1 and C2 at 71-82; AP as D (with D' and D-bar) at 233-245; the exact countable-signature conditions (nonempty, isomorphism closed, countably many isomorphism types, unbounded finite sizes, HP/JEP/AP) at 365-381 and def:p03-age-fraisse (classification-theory.tex 28-51); necessity of countably many types and unbounded sizes proved at annex 541-547.

Original increasing schedule: R_0 the empty restriction; stage p lists, for each representative B of size at most p, each restriction A of size at most p-1 and each embedding e: A -> R_{p-1}, the extension problem, a finite list solved by the finite-batch lemma (fraisse-1954.tex 247-271, annex 349-354, 367-379); chain-union well-definedness (fraisse-1954.tex 59-61, annex 11-15); exact age of the union and scheduling of every late problem via p >= max{m+1,|B|,|A|+1} (annex 381-393); countable-signature fair schedule of triples (i,A,e) with renaming and restriction to images, union countably infinite with Age(M)=K (annex 548-569).

Homogeneous implies H; H gives embeddings of countable A < R; back-and-forth with written forth and back steps (map kept when the point is already present), extension of any finite partial isomorphism, equal size for finite structures of one age; H equivalent to homogeneity on countable bases (fraisse-1954.tex 215-228, annex 288-318). Extension property of the constructed limit, uniqueness among countable homogeneous representatives and universality (annex 384-402); the same for the countable-signature limit (annex 571-579).

Explicit amalgams: arbitrary relations (mixed tuples set to minus), linear orders (gap-wise concatenation), partial orders (transitive closure with path compression and the Fig. 1 cross-side cycle) at fraisse-1954.tex 281-311 and annex 406-445; free graph amalgam at fraisse-1954.tex 416-435 and annex 627-635; the unary at-most-one-positive class having AP but not strong AP at annex 334-347. AP failure: ramified orders with the explicit four-point orders of Fig. 2 at fraisse-1954.tex 313-341 and annex 447-458. Structural maps distinguished from partial elementary maps at fraisse-1954.tex 210-212 and def:p03-ultrahomogeneous (classification-theory.tex 54-64, contrasting the elementary-map homogeneity definition).
